'''Gino Isidori''' (born 1968) is an [[Italians|Italian]] theoretical physicist, academic and author. He is a professor of [[Theoretical Physics]] at the [[University of Zurich]], where he also leads a research group,<ref name=aaa>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physik.uzh.ch/en/groups/isidori.html|title=Theory of Fundamental Interactions|website=www.physik.uzh.ch}}</ref> and is a member of the Science Policy Committee of the [[CERN]] Laboratory in [[Geneva]].<ref name=ccc>{{Cite web|url=https://council.web.cern.ch/en/content/membership-scientific-policy-committee|title=Membership of the Scientific Policy Committee &#124; CERN Council|website=council.web.cern.ch}}</ref>

Isidori is most known for his work on [[fundamental interactions]], including the [[Higgs boson]], the mechanism of [[quark]]-[[Flavour (particle physics)|flavor]] mixing, the [[metastability]] of the [[Standard Model]] vacuum, the hypotheses of Minimal Flavor Violation and Flavor Deconstruction, and theoretical predictions for rare particle processes.<ref name=ggg>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=NvEFgBMAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Gino Isidori|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> His publications comprise research articles and books including ''New Physics In B Decays'' and the chapter about Flavor Physics in ''The Standard Theory of Particle Physics''. He served as Editor-in-Chief for ''[[European Physical Journal C|The European Physics Journal C]]'' from 2011 to 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://epjc.epj.org/epjc-news/1290-epjc-new-editor-in-chief-for-theoretical-physics-i|title=The European Physical Journal C (EPJ C)|website=epjc.epj.org}}</ref> He has received awards such as the 2009 Hans Senior Fellowship from the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] of the [[Technical University of Munich]]<ref name=ttt>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ias.tum.de/en/ias/isidori-gino/|title=Isidori, Gino|website=www.ias.tum.de|date=19 May 2025 }}</ref> and the ERC Advanced Grant from the [[European Research Council]] in 2019.<ref name=eee>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physik.uzh.ch/en/news/News-2019/GinoIsidori_ERC.html|title=Gino Isidori ERC Grant|date=March 29, 2019|website=www.physik.uzh.ch}}</ref>

==Education and early career==
Isidori completed his undergraduate and graduate degrees at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]], followed by a PhD in [[Physics]] under the supervision of [[Luciano Maiani]] in 1996. He became a Visiting Scientist at the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory]] in 1997 and served as Postdoctoral Fellow at CERN from 2000 to 2002.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://physics.aps.org/authors/gino_isidori|title=Physics - Gino Isidori|website=physics.aps.org}}</ref>

==Career==
In 2000, Isidori assumed a research position at [[Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare|INFN]] Laboratories in [[Frascati]], which he held until 2014. He was appointed INFN Research Director in 2008, while also being a Guest Professor at [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa|Scuola Normale Superiore in Pisa]] (2007), a Senior Fellow at the Institute for Advanced Study at the Technical University of Munich (2009),<ref name=ttt/> and a Scientific Associate at CERN (2011–2013). Since 2014, he has held the position of Professor of Theoretical Physics in the Physics Department at the University of Zurich<ref name="aaa" /> and has been a member of the Science Policy Committee of the CERN Laboratory in Geneva since 2021.<ref name="ccc" />

Concurrently to his academic activity, he planned and featured in the [[YouTube]] series ''How Particle Theory Works'' (2018–2021), served as a Scientific Consultant for the TV movie ''[[Einstein (film)|Einstein]]'' (2007),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lilianacavani.it/en/productions/movies/einstein-2008/|title=Einstein (2008) – Liliana Cavani}}</ref> and participated in the outreach efforts of ''Scienza per Tutti'' magazine.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scienzapertutti.infn.it/che-cosa-e-la-materia-oscura?view=article&id=363:gino-isidori&catid=2|title=Scienza Per Tutti - Gino Isidori|website=scienzapertutti.infn.it}}</ref>

==Research==
Isidori has contributed to the field of theoretical physics by focusing on the theoretical and phenomenological investigation of fundamental interactions, formulating extensions of the Standard Model able to address its low-energy successes and resolve its theoretical issues above the TeV energy range.<ref name=ggg/> Before the discovery of the Higgs boson, with Giovanni Ridolfi and [[Alessandro Strumia]], he performed the first analysis of the stability of the Higgs potential beyond the semi-classical approximation.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1016/S0550-3213(01)00302-9|title=On the metastability of the standard model vacuum|date=2001 |doi=10.1016/S0550-3213(01)00302-9 |last1=Isidori |first1=Gino |last2=Ridolfi |first2=Giovanni |last3=Strumia |first3=Alessandro |journal=Nuclear Physics B |volume=609 |issue=3 |pages=387–409 |arxiv=hep-ph/0104016 |bibcode=2001NuPhB.609..387I }}</ref> By means of a further improvement of this analysis, after the discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 it was possible to demonstrate that the Standard Model ground state is not absolutely stable, but is sufficiently long-lived compared to the [[Age of the universe|age of the Universe]].<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP08(2012)098|title=Higgs mass and vacuum stability in the Standard Model at NNLO|first1=Giuseppe|last1=Degrassi|first2=Stefano|last2=Di Vita|first3=Joan|last3=Elias-Miró|first4=José R.|last4=Espinosa|first5=Gian F.|last5=Giudice|first6=Gino|last6=Isidori|first7=Alessandro|last7=Strumia|date=August 20, 2012|journal=Journal of High Energy Physics|volume=2012|issue=8|pages=98|doi=10.1007/JHEP08(2012)098|arxiv=1205.6497 |bibcode=2012JHEP...08..098D }}</ref>

Isidori played a key role in elucidating the mechanism of flavor mixing in extensions of the Standard Model, and its possible links to the origin of quark and lepton masses. In a collaborative study with [[Gian Giudice]] and others, he proposed the hypothesis of Minimal Flavor Violation (MFV) as a general mechanism to explain why precision measurements in B, D and K-meson physics do not reveal yet deviations from the Standard Model.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1016/S0550-3213(02)00836-2|title=Minimal flavor violation: An Effective field theory approach|date=2002 |doi=10.1016/S0550-3213(02)00836-2 |last1=d'Ambrosio |first1=G. |last2=Giudice |first2=G.F. |last3=Isidori |first3=G. |last4=Strumia |first4=A. |journal=Nuclear Physics B |volume=645 |issue=1–2 |pages=155–187 |arxiv=hep-ph/0207036 |bibcode=2002NuPhB.645..155D }}</ref> He also extended this concept to the lepton sector, linking the size of possible flavor violations in charged leptons to neutrino properties.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2005.08.037|title=Minimal flavor violation in the lepton sector|first1=Vincenzo|last1=Cirigliano|first2=Benjamín|last2=Grinstein|first3=Gino|last3=Isidori|first4=Mark B.|last4=Wise|date=November 30, 2005|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=728|issue=1–3|pages=121–134|doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2005.08.037|arxiv=hep-ph/0507001 |bibcode=2005NuPhB.728..121C }}</ref> Together with [[Riccardo Barbieri]] and others, in 2011, he demonstrated that an alternative to MFV is the hypothesis of a minimally broken U(2){{sup|3}}, a general framework to describe the quark-flavor structure of extensions of the Standard Model where third generation fermions plays a special role.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-011-1725-z|title=U(2) and minimal flavour violation in supersymmetry|first1=Riccardo|last1=Barbieri|first2=Gino|last2=Isidori|first3=Joel|last3=Jones-Pérez|first4=Paolo|last4=Lodone|first5=David M.|last5=Straub|date=August 18, 2011|journal=The European Physical Journal C|volume=71|issue=8|pages=1725|doi=10.1140/epjc/s10052-011-1725-z|arxiv=1105.2296 |bibcode=2011EPJC...71.1725B }}</ref> Beside proposing specific mechanisms to describe flavor violations in extensions of the Standard Model, he highlighted the relevance of flavor-violating processes in constraining the scale of new physics in general terms.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.annualreviews.org/doi/10.1146/annurev.nucl.012809.104534|title=Flavor Physics Constraints for Physics Beyond the Standard Model|first1=Gino|last1=Isidori|first2=Yosef|last2=Nir|first3=Gilad|last3=Perez|date=November 23, 2010|journal=Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science|volume=60|issue=1|pages=355–380|doi=10.1146/annurev.nucl.012809.104534|arxiv=1002.0900 |bibcode=2010ARNPS..60..355I }}</ref> In 2017, he introduced a three-site Pati–Salam gauge model to attempt to explain the origin of the flavor hierarchies, the quantization of the [[electric charge]], and the experimental hints of deviations from the Standard Model observed at that time in various B decays (so-called B anomalies).<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physletb.2018.02.011|title=A three-site gauge model for flavor hierarchies and flavor anomalies|first1=Marzia|last1=Bordone|first2=Claudia|last2=Cornella|first3=Javier|last3=Fuentes-Martín|first4=Gino|last4=Isidori|date=April 30, 2018|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=779|pages=317–323|doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2018.02.011|arxiv=1712.01368 |bibcode=2018PhLB..779..317B }}</ref> According to him, while the experimental significance of the B anomalies has diminished in the last few years, the idea of flavor non-universal gauge interactions, or Flavor Deconstruction, pioneered in the three-site Pati–Salam model has opened a new direction to address both the stability of the Higgs sector and the origin of quark and lepton mass hierarchies.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP07(2023)147|title=Non-universal gauge interactions addressing the inescapable link between Higgs and flavour|first1=Joe|last1=Davighi|first2=Gino|last2=Isidori|date=July 19, 2023|journal=Journal of High Energy Physics|volume=2023|issue=7|pages=147|doi=10.1007/JHEP07(2023)147|arxiv=2303.01520 |bibcode=2023JHEP...07..147D }}</ref>

Beside formulating hypotheses about [[physics beyond the Standard Model]], Isidori also contributed to precise estimates of various flavor-changing processes within the Standard Model. These include the precise assessment of radiative corrections in the tests of lepton flavor universality in <math>B \rightarrow K \ell^+</math> and <math>B \rightarrow K^* \ell^+ \ell^-</math> decays,<ref>{{Cite journal|title=On the standard model predictions for <math>R_K</math> and <math>R_{K^*}</math>|first1=Marzia|last1=Bordone|first2=Gino|last2=Isidori|first3=Andrea|last3=Pattori|date=August 8, 2016|journal=The European Physical Journal C|volume=76|issue=8|pages=440|doi=10.1140/epjc/s10052-016-4274-7|doi-access=free|arxiv=1605.07633}}</ref> the model-independent description of long-distance dynamics in <math>K^+ \rightarrow \pi^+ \ell^+ \ell^- </math> and <math>K_S \rightarrow \pi^0 \ell^+ \ell^- </math> decays,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1088/1126-6708/1998/08/004|title=The decays <math>K \rightarrow \pi \ell^+ \ell^-</math> beyond leading order in the chiral expansion|first1=Giancarlo|last1=D'Ambrosio|first2=Gerhard|last2=Ecker|first3=Gino|last3=Isidori|first4=Jorge|last4=Portolés|date=September 30, 1998|journal=Journal of High Energy Physics|volume=1998|issue=8|pages=004|doi=10.1088/1126-6708/1998/08/004|arxiv=hep-ph/9808289}}</ref>  and the estimate of non-perturbative contributions to <math>K \rightarrow \pi \nu \bar{\nu} </math>.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2005.04.008|title=Light-quark loops in <math>K \rightarrow \pi \nu \bar{\nu}</math> |doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2005.04.008 |arxiv=hep-ph/0503107 |last1=Isidori |first1=Gino |last2=Smith |first2=Christopher |last3=Mescia |first3=Federico |date=2005 }}</ref> He also  calculated non-perturbative corrections associated to charm re-scattering in <math>B \rightarrow X_s e^+ e^-</math> decays, <math>B \rightarrow X_s \gamma</math> and <math>B \rightarrow X_s \nu \bar{\nu}</math> decays, demonstrating that these effects can be controlled to a few % accuracy.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1016/S0550-3213(97)00674-3|title=Corrections of order to inclusive rare B decays|first1=G.|last1=Buchalla|first2=G.|last2=Isidori|first3=S.-J.|last3=Rey|date=February 28, 1998|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=511|issue=3|pages=594–610|doi=10.1016/s0550-3213(97)00674-3|arxiv=hep-ph/9705253}}</ref>
